mainTopic: Why the כהן גדול's seven-day separation before יום הכפורים is learned from the מילואים, and not from שמיני עצרת, שבועות, or ראש השנה
overview: Earlier, the גמרא learned the seven-day separation of the כהן גדול before יום הכפורים from the seven days of the מילואים. It also explained why the separation is not learned from שמיני עצרת: that day is a make-up day for the first day of סוכות. The amud opens with פז"ר קש"ב, a memory aid that admits שמיני עצרת is its own holiday in six ways. For תשלומין (making up missed offerings), though, it is still part of סוכות, so it is still excluded. Next the גמרא asks why we don't learn from שבועות. רבי אבא answers that יום הכפורים and the מילואים both have one bull and one ram, while שבועות has two rams. A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון holds יום הכפורים also has two rams. The גמרא answers that even so, only one of them belongs to the day's own obligation. Then the גמרא suggests ראש השנה, and רבי אבהו says the comparison is to the כהן's own bull and ram, not community offerings. The amud ends by starting to question whether 'קח לך' really means 'from your own'. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A memory aid: שמיני עצרת is its own holiday
steps.stepSummary: The answer about שמיני עצרת ends with the acronym פז"ר קש"ב, which lists six ways שמיני עצרת stands as a separate holiday from סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: P-Z-R K-Sh-B (פייס, זמן, רגל, קרבן, שירה, ברכה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concedes part of the challenge with a memory aid. The acronym lists six areas where שמיני עצרת really is a separate holiday. The next step shows the area where it is not separate, and that is what keeps it out of the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each letter stands for a separate feature. פייס: a new lottery for the כהנים. זמן: we say שהחיינו. רגל: it is a holiday of its own. קרבן: its offerings are counted fresh. שירה: the לויים sing a new song. ברכה: the holiday insert in תפילה and ברכת המזון is worded differently. These six points grant that שמיני עצרת is independent in these areas. They are not the reason it is excluded from the comparison. That reason comes in the next step (תשלומין).

keyTerms.meaning: Memory acronym: פַּיִס, זְמַן, רֶגֶל, קָרְבָּן, שִׁירָה, בְּרָכָה
The eighth-day holiday right after סוכות
A holiday standing on its own
The lottery used to assign Temple jobs to the כהנים

phrases.english: P-Z-R K-Sh-B (Lottery, Time-blessing, Festival, Offering, Song, Blessing).
phrases.notes: Six ways שמיני עצרת is a holiday of its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer, begun on the previous amud, to the challenge from שמיני עצרת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the comparison case is really an independent unit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since שמיני עצרת is a holiday in its own right, it seems it should not be excluded as merely secondary to סוכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גמרא grants that שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday in six ways (פז"ר קש"ב). The next step limits this: for תשלומין it is still part of סוכות.

steps.title: One way שמיני עצרת does count with סוכות: making up missed offerings
steps.stepSummary: Even though שמיני עצרת is a separate holiday, it still counts as a make-up day for the חגיגה offering of סוכות. This is proven from a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, regarding make-up offerings, it is a make-up day for the first holiday. As we learned in a משנה: one who did not bring the holiday offering on the first day of the festival may keep bringing it the whole festival, including the last holiday day of the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to what it just said. In one area, תשלומין (making up a missed offering), שמיני עצרת is still connected to סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who missed bringing his חגיגה on the first day of סוכות may make it up later. The משנה says he can do so until 'the last holiday day of the festival,' which means שמיני עצרת. So for תשלומין, שמיני עצרת is an extension of the first day of סוכות. That is why it cannot serve as a model for the מילואים, even though in the six areas of פז"ר קש"ב it is separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Make-up time for a missed holiday offering
Here: brought the חֲגִיגָה offering
For we learned in a מִשְׁנָה
May keep bringing the offering

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a side note. It is the real answer. The six features of פז"ר קש"ב were a concession. What matters for the comparison is that, for תשלומין, שמיני עצרת is tied to the first day of סוכות, so it is excluded.

phrases.english: But regarding make-up offerings,
it is a make-up day for the first (holiday),
as we learned in a משנה:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג —
phrases.english: one who did not bring the holiday offering on the first day of the festival —
may keep bringing it throughout the entire festival,
and on the last holiday day of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 1: in one area, שמיני עצרת is linked to סוכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For תשלומין, שמיני עצרת counts as a make-up day for סוכות.

steps.title: Challenge: why not learn the separation from שבועות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a new source: שבועות (עצרת) is also one day after a stretch of weekdays. Perhaps the כהן גדול should be separated before שבועות instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is learned from עצרת (שבועות), which is also a separation of seven days for one day!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that שמיני עצרת has been ruled out, the גמרא raises another possible model: שבועות. It too is a single holiday day that could have seven days of separation before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that we only need some 'seven days before one day' model. שבועות is a one-day holiday, and unlike שמיני עצרת it is not a make-up day (תשלומין) for an earlier holiday. So the reason that ruled out שמיני עצרת does not rule out שבועות.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (instead)…
In חז"ל's language, this usually means שָׁבוּעוֹת
A seven-day separation

steps.confusionAlert: Here עצרת means שבועות, not שמיני עצרת. חז"ל commonly call שבועות 'עצרת.'

phrases.english: But say (we learn from) Atzeret (שבועות),
which is a separation of seven days for one day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting שמיני עצרת, the גמרא suggests another possible model.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the separation before יום הכפורים is learned specifically from the מילואים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבועות also fits the pattern of seven days before one day, so why not learn from it?

steps.title: רבי אבא: match one bull and one ram to one bull and one ram
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that we compare יום הכפורים to the מילואים because both bring exactly one bull and one ram. שבועות brings two rams, so it is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: We learn 'one bull and one ram' from 'one bull and one ram,' which excludes עצרת, since it has two rams.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא gives the reason the מילואים is the right source and שבועות is not. The offerings must match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison rests on a shared detail in the offerings. On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול brings one bull and one ram, and so did the מילואים. שבועות includes two rams, so its offerings do not match, and it cannot be the source.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive / compare
A bull
A ram
To exclude

phrases.english: רבי אבא said:
we derive (a case of) one bull and one ram
from (a case of) one bull and one ram,
phrases.notes: Here יום הכפורים is learned from the case of the מילואים.

phrases.english: which excludes Atzeret (שבועות),
since there are two rams.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: דָּנִין פַּר אֶחָד וְאַיִל אֶחָד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on matching offering details
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any 'seven days before one day' holiday, like שבועות, could serve as the model.
steps.terutzMaskana: The model must match in offerings: one bull and one ram. Only the מילואים fits.

steps.title: Challenge: what about the view that יום הכפורים has two rams?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא's answer. It works only for the opinion that יום הכפורים has one ram. According to the opinion that it has two rams, the match breaks down.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says יום הכפורים has one ram. But according to the one who says there are two rams, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אבא's answer. It points out that his answer depends on a disputed fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יום הכפורים has two rams, then it no longer matches the מילואים' one ram. In fact, it would look more like שבועות, which also has two rams. So according to that opinion, the reason for picking the מילואים over שבועות disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well
According to the one who says
What can be said?

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
(that on) יום הכפורים there is one ram,
but according to the one who says
that there are two rams,
what can be said?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים אַיִל אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אבא's answer from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's 'one bull and one ram' comparison
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If יום הכפורים has two rams, it does not match the מילואים, so the reason to exclude שבועות falls away.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a dispute over one ram or two on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the two-ram opinion is real. רבי says the ram in ויקרא and the ram in במדבר are the same ram. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון says they are two separate rams.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: one ram. The one mentioned here (ויקרא) is the same one mentioned in the book of במדבר. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון says: there are two rams, one mentioned here and one mentioned in the book of במדבר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge by quoting a ברייתא. It shows that there really is an opinion that יום הכפורים has two rams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה mentions a ram for יום הכפורים in two places: ויקרא 16 (the כהן גדול's עולה) and במדבר 29 (the holiday מוסף). רבי reads them as one and the same ram. רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון reads them as two different rams. His view is what makes the challenge to רבי אבא so strong.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a בְּרַיְיתָא
The book of בְּמִדְבַּר (the book of the counts)
The one mentioned here (in וַיִּקְרָא 16)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבא's answer (match one bull and one ram) works easily according to רבי. According to רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון, יום הכפורים has two rams, so the comparison needs defending. The next step defends it.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says:
one ram: the one mentioned here (in ויקרא)
is the same one mentioned in the book of במדבר.
רבי אליעזר son of רבי שמעון says:
they are two rams,
one mentioned here (in ויקרא),
and one mentioned in the book of במדבר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the two-ram opinion that the challenge in step 5 relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an opinion holding יום הכפורים has two rams
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute between רבי and רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון

steps.title: Even with two rams, יום הכפורים is still different from שבועות
steps.stepSummary: Even according to רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון, the two rams of יום הכפורים have two different jobs. One is for the special service of the day and one is for the מוסף. On שבועות, both rams are for the day's own obligation. So שבועות still does not match.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this fits רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון. There, on יום הכפורים, one ram is for the obligation of the day, and one is for the additional offerings. That leaves out שבועות, where both rams are the obligation of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 5. It shows that רבי אבא's comparison still works even for the opinion that יום הכפורים has two rams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that if יום הכפורים has two rams, it looks just like שבועות. The answer: what counts is how many rams belong to the day's own special obligation. On יום הכפורים, only one ram does, because the other is a regular מוסף. On שבועות, both rams are part of the day's obligation, so the 'one bull, one ram' match with the מילואים still holds only for יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (the answer works even for this opinion)
The special obligation of the day itself
The additional offerings brought on שבת and holidays
To exclude; this leaves out
שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is denying that יום הכפורים has two rams according to רבי אליעזר ברבי שמעון. It accepts that there are two rams. It only says they serve different roles, so for this comparison only one of them counts.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Shimon:
there (on Yom Kippur), one ram is for the obligation of the day,
and one is for the additional offerings.
phrases.notes: The ram in במדבר is part of the regular holiday מוסף.

phrases.english: This excludes Shavuot,
where both rams are the obligation of the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Steps 5-6 by refining רבי אבא's comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the comparison: count only the ram that belongs to the day's own obligation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two rams on יום הכפורים would make it look exactly like שבועות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one ram on יום הכפורים is חובת היום. The second is a מוסף. On שבועות both are חובת היום, so שבועות is still excluded.

steps.title: Maybe we should learn from ראש השנה instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests ראש השנה as another possible source. It also comes after seven regular days, and it also has one bull and one ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say we learn it from ראש השנה, since there too it would be a separation of seven days for one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new candidate. Maybe the כהן גדול should be separated for seven days before ראש השנה, since it seems to fit the מילואים pattern too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike שבועות, the מוסף of ראש השנה has exactly one bull and one ram. So the 'one bull, one ram' test from Steps 4 and 7 does not rule it out. It also comes after a stretch of weekdays. The גמרא needs a new reason to exclude it.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (proposes an alternative)
The holiday of the new year
Separation; setting the כהן apart before the service

phrases.english: But say it applies to Rosh HaShana,
since it is a separation of seven days for one day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After שבועות is excluded, the גמרא proposes a different holiday that passes the 'one bull, one ram' test.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יום הכפורים is the only holiday that matches the מילואים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ראש השנה also has one bull and one ram and also comes after weekdays. So the comparison should apply to it as well.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the comparison is about the כהן's own bull and ram
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says we compare offerings that the כהן brings from his own property. On יום הכפורים and at the מילואים, the bull and ram belong to the כהן. On שבועות and ראש השנה, they belong to the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: We learn a bull and a ram that are his own from a bull and a ram that were his own. That excludes שבועות and ראש השנה, whose offerings belong to the community.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a sharper rule for the comparison. The bull and ram must be the כהן's own personal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכפורים, the כהן גדול brings his bull and ram from his own money. At the מילואים, אהרן's bull and ram were his own. The bull and ram of ראש השנה and שבועות are community offerings, so they don't match. This one rule knocks out both ראש השנה and שבועות.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or derive (one case from another)
A bull and a ram
His own; belonging to the כהן personally
The community; offerings paid for by the public

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison between יום הכפורים and the מילואים is based on the כהן's OWN bull and ram. Community offerings on other holidays don't count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
We derive a bull and a ram that are his own (on Yom Kippur)
from a bull and a ram that were his own (at the inauguration).
This excludes Shavuot and Rosh HaShana,
since those offerings belong to the community.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: דָּנִין פָּר וָאַיִל שֶׁלּוֹ מִפָּר וָאַיִל שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ראש השנה challenge with a new rule for the comparison: ownership.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New basis for the comparison: who owns the offerings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ראש השנה matches because it has one bull and one ram.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the כהן's own bull and ram count. ראש השנה and שבועות have community offerings, so they are excluded.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge: does 'קח לך' mean from your own property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to question רבי אבהו's answer. His answer works for the opinion that 'קח לך' means 'from your own'. The challenge for the other opinion continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says 'קח לך' ('take for yourself') means 'from your own property'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It hints that רבי אבהו's answer only works according to one opinion, and the full challenge comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו assumed that אהרן's bull and ram at the מילואים were his own. That is true only if the Torah's words 'קח לך' mean 'take from your own money'. If someone reads 'קח לך' differently, for example as coming from community funds, then the מילואים offerings were not אהרן's own. In that case, רבי אבהו's comparison would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (usually followed by 'but according to the other view, there is a problem')
According to the one who says
'Take for yourself', the Torah's wording at the מילואים
From your own property

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not finished. 'הניחא' only tells us the answer works for one opinion. The actual problem, according to the other opinion, comes right on the next amud.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
that 'Take for yourself' means from your own property,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to challenge רבי אבהו's answer by questioning whether the מילואים offerings were really אהרן's own.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's claim that the מילואים bull and ram were the כהן's own property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The claim works only if 'קח לך' means 'from your own'. For the opinion that reads it otherwise, the ownership comparison breaks down. This part continues on the next amud.
